entry.title: Social Summary: November 13, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic's IPO filing was the day's landmark business story. The Jensen Huang resignation saga at Nvidia drove the sharpest debate.

  • Demis Hassabis and Logan Kilpatrick positioned Hydrogen as the fast everyday tier, claiming 2.5x faster task completion and a slim edge over Gemini 4 Argon, with broad free availability
  • Huang reactions split: Marcus argued the criticism is about China policy and security exposure, not personal conduct; Casey Newton called it the end of a cavalier era; Clement Delangue defended Nvidia's structure and stayed bullish
  • Fei-Fei Li opened World Labs' Atlas world model to everyone; Anthropic launched self-hosted Managed Agents in private beta, targeting data-control-sensitive enterprises

  • An unverified forensic claim by a former OpenAI researcher regarding DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax circulated widely but lacked confirmation

Weights are open on Hugging Face.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Governance shock dominated the day: Casey Newton amplified a WSJ report that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang — the batch's highest-scored and most consequential story, though still unconfirmed.

  • AI-for-science had a strong day: Demis Hassabis announced AlphaGenome 2 for predicting DNA variant effects across cell types, and DeepMind claimed the first code-level formal security proof of Signal's protocol.
  • Google launched Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/1M tokens, with Artificial Analysis independently reporting a leading 66 score on its Decision Index v2.1.
  • Open robotics momentum: Runway released Praxis-1 under Apache 2.0, while Jim Fan demoed GR00T 2 autonomously running a chemistry-lab experiment.
  • Ethan Mollick argued coding's AI transformation is far ahead of public perception; Matt Shumer shared a 400B-token Claude Fable 5.2 guide, and the Perplexity CEO showed a Teammate agent building a game autonomously.
  • Perplexity published red-teaming findings on its open-source SPACE sandbox; former White House advisor Ben Buchanan argued China could lead in AI absent chip export controls.
  • Ecosystem funding: UK chip startup Fractile raised $720M at a ~$7B valuation; n8n shipped an open-source personal agent claiming 98% task completion.

entry.title:
New research on red teaming our sandbox platform SPACE:
1. CTF red-teaming should prompt explicitl...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas shares new research on red-teaming Perplexity's open-source sandbox platform SPACE, reporting five findings: CTF red-teaming requires explicit prompting to break host-guest isolation; non-cyber models (e.g., GPT-5.6 Sol) outperformed cyber-specialized variants (GPT-5.6 Sol Cyber) at finding exploits; the platform withstood sandbox isolation exploits; a DNS spoofing network bypass was discovered and fixed; and findings are being shared openly with the agent sandbox and security community.

entry.summary: Ethan Mollick clarifies that his prior remarks were neither AI hype nor doom: he argues there is a limited window to shape the AI transition so professions improve while remaining human-centered, and that ignoring reality will not achieve that.

entry.title: @TimDarcet @gabriberton The P in JEPA stands for predictive. The main distinction is not between JEA...
entry.summary: LeCun continues yesterday's Social thread, adding formal loss formulations and the history of anti-collapse methods. Yann LeCun (@ylecun) responds to a discussion by clarifying the taxonomy of joint-embedding architectures: the P in JEPA stands for predictive, and the fundamental distinction is not between JEA and JEPA but between joint-embedding approaches (predictive or not) and generative architectures. He lays out formal loss formulations: generative models predict y from x with a divergence loss between target and prediction, while JEA encodes both x and y and minimizes representation divergence with an anti-collapse regularizer R, useful when neither view has a privileged direction (e.g., two views of the same scene). He adds historical depth, citing Becker and Hinton's 1989 information-maximization anti-collapse model and noting Schmidhuber's early related work, and notes that whether a predictor is needed depends on the task.
